Subject: HealthByte security questionnaire - PII export & key custody follow-ups

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looks promising. We've started our SSQ and have a couple of clarifying asks about how Redwood treats exported PII and cryptographic key custody for EU-hosted workloads. I attached the partial SSQ (sheet: "export_kms_questions"). High level asks:

- If a customer pins a model in the eu-west region but requests an export (e.g., for analytics) that crosses borders, what controls exist to prevent inadvertent transfer of raw PII?
- Do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) for model store artifacts and audit logs? If yes: where are keys stored (Redwood KMS, customer KMS via KMS proxy, HSM)?
- For short-lived export jobs, can we require tokenization/pseudonymization hooks prior to any persistence outside eu-west? Is that a supported pipeline step today or a recommended integration pattern?

Can you please assign a technical point-of-contact who can confirm whether KMS key material ever leaves the EU boundary for managed deployments?

Thanks,
Sara
Security Program Manager | HealthByte

From: priya_natarajan@redwood.com

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (privacy lead) and Karthik (applied ML / infra) to ensure we cover both compliance and runtime behaviors. Short answers up front:

- Exports: by default, model outputs and artifacts are stored in the region where the request was processed. Cross-border exports require an explicit export job and are gated by ACLs and audit trails; we also have an export pipeline where customers can opt for in-region processing only.
- CMK: we support customer-managed encryption keys for storage artifacts and audit logs via customer KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Google KMS). For Private deployments we can integrate with customer HSMs.
- Tokenization hooks: we do not automatically tokenise payloads before export, but we provide pre-export webhooks and a transform step that teams can use to apply pseudonymization. We can provide a short-runbook for plug-in with a tokenization service.

Karthik — can you confirm whether any key material is proxied outside of eu-west for hosted eu workloads? Also attaching our initial diagram (redwood-kms-keyflow-v1.png) and a matrix showing how we segment PII in logs.

— Priya
Product Security | Redwood Inference

Hi Sara — quick policy note from the privacy side:

- For any account that requires EU-only residency we recommend enabling the eu-region residency flag and enforcing the "region-lock exports" policy in the Console; this prevents ad-hoc exports from the UI or API unless an admin explicitly authorizes them (we capture justification and require two approvers).
- We can include a DPA annex clause specifying that Redwood will not transfer PII outside the EU except per documented, auditable export requests. If HealthByte needs SCCs or UK Addendum language, we have templates (happy to iterate).
- For audit evidence we can provide: export approval logs, per-export manifest, and a redaction/tokenization checksum that proves a transform was applied prior to export.

Priya / Karthik — if possible, can we produce a short evidence packet (logs + diagram + the transform runbook) for HealthByte by EOD Thursday? Sara, if that works I will send the DPA annex template for review.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Privacy | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@healthbyte.ai>
Date: 2026-04-14T11:47:00Z
Subject: Re: HealthByte security questionnaire - PII export & key custody follow-ups

Sara — technical confirmation below. Short version: no key material leaves the EU for "hosted eu" workloads when configured with customer KMS or Redwood-managed EU keys. Details:

- Key storage and wrapping: For customer-managed keys we integrate via a KMS proxy that performs remote Wrap/Unwrap operations; the raw key material never leaves the customer's KMS. For Redwood-managed keys restricted to eu-west we store key material in an EU HSM cluster (we use a regional HSM service with EU-only zones).
- Audit logs: all wrap/unwrap API calls are logged in-region; logs contain only metadata (key id, operation, timestamp) — not raw key material.
- Exports & transforms: We have a pre-export transform pipeline that can be configured to run a Python lambda (sandboxed) inside the eu region. That lambda can call a tokenization microservice (customer-managed or our recommended partner). We record a transform checksum (SHA256) in the export manifest.
- Edge cases: telemetry traces (for performance debugging) are sampled and can be configured to drop payloads containing PII fields; by default we do not store request payloads beyond short-lived caches.

I attached the PII segmentation matrix we discussed and a short runbook snippet for the tokenization hook. If HealthByte wants, we can schedule a 30-minute tech walkthrough next week to walk through the KMS proxy flow.

— Karthik
Staff Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
